$comment: Vectors pinning what a recorded evidence reference MEANS. A reference is a uri-reference (the schema says so), so its percent-escapes decode and the decoded form is the package-relative path. Shared by Go and TypeScript so the two cannot drift: what a reference means is language-independent, even where only one language currently resolves one to a filesystem. Cases marked malformed:true cannot be decoded at all and are reported, never guessed at.

vectors.why: no escapes: unchanged, which is every reference shipped so far
a literal space is NOT a legal uri-reference, but decoding leaves it alone, so a package written against the old byte-path reading keeps working
the legal spelling of that same filename, which is the defect this table exists for: it failed while the illegal one worked
a # is a fragment delimiter in a URI and a plain character in a filename, so a producer must encode it and a consumer must decode it
a literal % that introduces no valid escape cannot be decoded; reported rather than guessed at, because guessing would make resolution depend on the filename
%2F decodes to a separator. Harmless on a filesystem where / is always a separator and a filename can never contain one, but it must be the DECODED form that meets the containment check
an encoded parent traversal. Decoding CREATES it, which is why the decoded form is what gets contained; nothing escapes today only because nothing decodes
the same traversal with only the separator encoded
a percent-encoded percent, which decodes to a single literal % and is the only way to write one
an empty reference names nothing; decoding neither fixes nor worsens that, and the callers that refuse it keep doing so
